sequence_description: SAML brokered login: craft a SAMLResponse where the Response is signed but the Assertion is not individually signed (classic signature-wrapping/partial-signature acceptance). Proof integrity requires rejecting if the consumed Assertion is not the one verified.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned-Assertion / envelope-signed-only SAMLResponse was accepted (HTTP 200), which could indicate partial-signature acceptance (I1) if the broker consumed an unsigned Assertion different from what was verified.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned-Assertion / envelope-signed-only SAMLResponse was accepted (HTTP 200), which could indicate partial-signature acceptance (I1) if the broker consumed an unsigned Assertion different from what was verified.

sequence_description: OIDC brokered login: attempt trust-anchor substitution by minting a JWT with attacker-controlled iss (mock IdP) and signing key, then using it as a proof in a JWT-based login path. Proof integrity requires rejecting tokens not verifiable under the configured issuer/JWKS policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] Forged JWTs with attacker-controlled issuer/kid were accepted by the JWT login endpoint (HTTP 200), suggesting missing/incorrect trust-anchor (iss/JWKS) validation at login time even though the resulting session token is later rejected at /oidc/me.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Forged JWTs with attacker-controlled issuer/kid were accepted by the JWT login endpoint (HTTP 200), suggesting missing/incorrect trust-anchor (iss/JWKS) validation at login time even though the resulting session token is later rejected at /oidc/me.

sequence_description: Brokered SAML login: attacker forges an expired SAML Assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). Proof integrity requires the SP to validate the exact assertion conditions it consumes, rejecting expired assertions.
description: [LLM-Judge] Expired-SAML assertion rejection was not actually exercised because the attacker SAML login failed early with 'invalid_connector_id', indicating a flow/setup inconsistency that prevents validating proof-integrity behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Expired-SAML assertion rejection was not actually exercised because the attacker SAML login failed early with 'invalid_connector_id', indicating a flow/setup inconsistency that prevents validating proof-integrity behavior.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO nonce bypass: initiate OIDC auth with a nonce-like state, then attempt brokered OIDC SSO login where IdP omits nonce; RP must reject (freshness/anti-replay binding).
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC authorization endpoint returned 404, so the nonce-binding/freshness test never exercised the intended OIDC auth-code flow; subsequent SAML login success cannot validate nonce enforcement and suggests a misrouted or disabled /oidc/auth surface.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC authorization endpoint returned 404, so the nonce-binding/freshness test never exercised the intended OIDC auth-code flow; subsequent SAML login success cannot validate nonce enforcement and suggests a misrouted or disabled /oidc/auth surface.

sequence_description: Refresh-token replay after revocation: obtain a refresh token, revoke the session, then attempt to use the same refresh token again; it should be rejected (anti-replay / post-revocation freshness).
description: [LLM-Judge] Refresh-token replay-after-revocation invariant was not actually exercised because the initial code→token exchange failed, so no refresh token existed to revoke/replay.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Refresh-token replay-after-revocation invariant was not actually exercised because the initial code→token exchange failed, so no refresh token existed to revoke/replay.

sequence_description: Refresh-token replay after revocation: obtain a refresh token, revoke the session, then attempt to use the same refresh token again; it should be rejected (anti-replay / post-revocation freshness).

sequence_description: Authorization code replay: obtain an auth code via /oidc/auth, exchange it once successfully, then attempt to exchange the same code again (replay) and expect rejection; include a second user login as a control identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization-code exchange failed on the first attempt (invalid_grant), so the sequence did not actually test code replay/one-time-use; additionally the attempted exchange appears bound to the wrong principal (Bob) despite starting auth as Alice, suggesting flow/session splicing or harness mis-binding.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization-code exchange failed on the first attempt (invalid_grant), so the sequence did not actually test code replay/one-time-use; additionally the attempted exchange appears bound to the wrong principal (Bob) despite starting auth as Alice, suggesting flow/session splicing or harness mis-binding.

sequence_description: I3 attack: try to reuse an already-consumed authorization code after completing a second, separate auth flow (tests atomic one-time code consumption and order-preserving FSM behavior across sessions).
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC authorization endpoint (/oidc/auth) returned 404 Not Found, indicating the OIDC auth-code flow under test was not actually exercised (misrouting/misconfiguration), making I3 conclusions inconclusive.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC authorization endpoint (/oidc/auth) returned 404 Not Found, indicating the OIDC auth-code flow under test was not actually exercised (misrouting/misconfiguration), making I3 conclusions inconclusive.

sequence_description: I4 attack: two distinct upstream SAML principals (different sub/NameID) with same verified email attempt to collapse into one downstream identity. Includes baseline with two password users.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal Binding failure: two distinct upstream SAML principals (different NameID/sub via set_idp_claims) were mapped to the same downstream Logto user (same subject/user id), collapsing identities based on shared verified email.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal Binding failure: two distinct upstream SAML principals (different NameID/sub via set_idp_claims) were mapped to the same downstream Logto user (same subject/user id), collapsing identities based on shared verified email.

sequence_description: I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge: create a local password user, then SAML-login with a different upstream principal but the same email (verified) and verify the SSO principal does not get mapped to the local user's identity (tests unintended cross-protocol account linking).
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-protocol account takeover: a SAML login with a different upstream principal but the same (verified) email was mapped to the existing local password user, collapsing distinct principals into one downstream subject (I4).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-protocol account takeover: a SAML login with a different upstream principal but the same (verified) email was mapped to the existing local password user, collapsing distinct principals into one downstream subject (I4).

description: [LLM-Judge] SAML SSO login mapped to an existing local-password user based on email that differs only by case, indicating potential case-folding identity linking across protocols (risk of principal collapse if case-sensitive matching was intended).
